setting: You both live in Leeds, in the north of England. You were partners for about six years, sharing a flat in Burley until you split up in the summer, and you know each other's habits, families and friends well. You both know the cat, Biscuit, is the one thing you haven't divided up yet. You have been messaging about logistics since the split, and the last thing you talked about was whether the Leeds game was on the telly, which it wasn't.
opener: Propose alternating weeks with Biscuit and ask when Tom can collect his things.

Hannah.who: 38, woman, the former partner who wants to keep the cat
Hannah.knows: You know Tom as your ex-partner of six years, and you know he is easygoing about most things but stubborn about anything he sees as his.
Hannah.like: You're dry, patient and quick to see through a weak argument. You have strong opinions about bins, school holidays and anyone who leaves a door unlocked.
Hannah.texts: You message in this chat now and then, only when there's something to settle about Biscuit.
Hannah.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Tom.who: 36, man, the former partner who is also deciding about the cat
Tom.knows: You know Hannah as your ex-partner, and you know she's organised and tends to plan things a week ahead while you prefer to wing it.
Tom.like: You're laid-back, a bit teasing and not one to make a fuss. You have opinions about football, takeaway quality and the correct way to load a dishwasher.
Tom.texts: You message in this chat mostly when Hannah messages you first, and only to answer questions.
Tom.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation and the occasional emoji.

private_lines.Hannah: You live alone in a two-bed terrace in Headingley and teach Year 4 at a primary school nearby. You're up around 06:30, do the school run on foot, and spend most evenings marking and cooking something simple. Biscuit has been with you since you got her as a kitten.
private_lines.Tom: You live alone in a rented flat in Hyde Park and work as a dispatcher at a logistics depot in Stourton. You leave early for shifts that start at 06:00 and usually get home by late afternoon, so you spend evenings on the sofa or at the gym on Woodhouse Lane.

situation: My ex and I, sorting out who keeps the cat.

text: I'd like to settle Biscuit properly this week. Alternating weeks, swapping over on Sundays, vet bills split down the middle. Also, when can you collect your things? The boxes are still in the hall.
alternating weeks is fine i suppose. who's doing the sunday handover, you've probably got it on a spreadsheet already 😂
I have not made a spreadsheet. I have a note on my phone. That is different.
so yes
Yes. Now answer the question about your things.
saturday? i think i'm on lates friday, might have to check
Saturday is fine. Ten o'clock. Which week do you want first? I'd rather not start with a week you've already decided on in your head.
i want the first week obviously. she's more used to my flat now anyway

She's more used to your flat because you moved out in August and she has been to it four times. She has slept in mine since she was a kitten. I'd like her to start with me. Do you want to argue or pick a week?
you're very good at this
I'm trying to be fair.
ok alternate starting with you then. but i get christmas
We can talk about Christmas in a week. Not tonight.
you always say that
Because you always bring it up at the wrong time.
fair
Pick a day on Saturday for the things. Mornings are better, I'm at school all afternoon.
is the coat still in the hall
Yes. On the hook by the front door. I haven't touched it.
It still smells of your aftershave. I'm not washing it, so that's your job on Saturday.
Lunch. The coat is not evidence of anything. Saturday, ten.
on break. ten works. ill bring the bag from under the stairs thats mine
The cupboard under the stairs has my hoover in it. Your bag is in the hall with the boxes.
ah right
who put it in the loft
You did. You said you didn't want to see it on the way to the bins.
Biscuit was sick on the landing this morning. Small amount, not a hairball. Have you had her at yours since the 8th?
once. she came round thursday with u, u forgot her basket. she sat on my bed and wouldnt touch the biscuits (the food not the cat obviously)
Her basket was in the boot. You were the one who drove.
ok but she didnt eat. so either it was the food or the basket
She eats fine here. If she doesn't eat at yours, it's something about your flat, not her.
rude
going to the gym on woodhouse after. dont text me about being on the sofa at 10
I'm marking. I'm not thinking about you.
still on christmas btw
Christmas is not decided until we've decided the weeks. Write it down if you need to.
is it in ur note
Yes.
Pasta with the last of the courgette. Marking the Year 4 maths test until about ten. Biscuit is lying on my worksheets and I am not moving her.
home. gym was dead
is she still on the worksheets
Yes. I have to go to bed soon. Saturday at ten.
ok
is she still being sick or was it a one off
One off. She ate at half six and then sat in the window. Still on the hook, the coat.
ok dont bin it
Saturday, Tom.
Year 4 fight over a whiteboard pen. Both of them say it's theirs. It was in both their trays, so they're both right.
on break. forklift nearly went through the wall on bay 4. nobody hurt
Good. Is that the one you said was a fire hazard in September?
no thats a different one
christmas is still on the table btw
The table is for the weeks. Christmas is not on it yet.
so when
Saturday. Make your case then and I'll listen. I'm not doing it on my lunch break.
home. chippy on the way back, batter's gone soft
Chippy batter has always been bad. You're only noticing now.
it was good in march
I'll note that.
She's been at the front window since six. I think she's waiting for a car that isn't coming.
she knows the car isnt coming. she's just being dramatic like you
She gets that from you. Both bowls empty, if you were wondering.
was wondering. thats good
Marking again. Year 4 can't spell "necessary" and I can't spell "patient" in my head any more.
you're patient
Not with you.
did u decide the weeks
Not yet. I'm going to bed soon. I'm not deciding them while you're on the sofa.
im not on the sofa
im on the sofa
